solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Leader having lost power, living somewhere

indicators.note: something lost is gone, so a letter standing for the following word is dropped from the leader

parts.note: a president is a national leader
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A deposed head of state now just lives somewhere quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: Take P from PRESIDENT to leave RESIDENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident is a person who dwells in a particular place, an adjective-like noun matching the phrase.

clue.text: Trace that's survived in unexpected manner over time

indicators.note: in a down answer, over means placed above, so the first part sits on top of the second
something unexpected comes out differently from the norm, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Something has come through the years in a surprising way.
explanation.definitionFit: A remnant is a small leftover part, a lingering trace of what once existed.

clue.text: At home in safe job, well-paid and undemanding

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the next, so one word is put within the other

parts.note: secure means safe
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: Someone at home is content in a cushy, secure, well-paid post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At home' reads as part of the surface scene, but here it is the inserted piece; the definition runs from 'job' to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a post giving income or status for little real work, the classic cushy number.

clue.text: Need ground to embrace supporter's song, magical

indicators.note: an embrace wraps arms around someone, so one piece goes around the other
ground means crushed and broken up, so these letters are reformed in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a football supporter's song from the terraces is a chant

explanation.surface: A football ground ought to welcome a fan's spellbinding song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like a stadium, but it is the past tense of grind; the shuffled letters split in two around the song.
explanation.definitionFit: Enchanted means under a spell, bewitched, which is the adjective magical.

clue.text: Secure neckwear

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to fasten with a knot
second meaning: a strip of cloth knotted at the collar

explanation.surface: An instruction to fasten something worn at the throat.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means fasten or bind; as a noun it is the necktie worn with a shirt.

clue.text: Information about lake valley

indicators.note: one thing placed about another wraps around it, so the first word surrounds the second

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone asks for facts about a lakeside valley.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN goes around L to make GLEN; gen is informal British English for the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: A glen is a narrow valley, especially in Scotland, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Linguistic rules diagram Mary keeps

indicators.note: the preceding words hold the letters within them, the way a box keeps its contents

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A girl holds onto a chart of language rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar is the system of structural rules governing a language.

clue.text: Media boss provided dessert in building

parts.note: ED is short for editor, who runs a newspaper
if means provided that
an ice is a frozen dessert

explanation.surface: An editor laid on pudding at the office.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large, imposing building.

clue.text: List of options guys use initially

parts.note: guys are men

indicators.note: initially points at the start, so only the opening letter of the preceding word is used

parts.note: first letter of use

explanation.surface: A list of options that blokes rely on from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu offers choices, whether dishes in a restaurant or commands on a computer screen.

clue.text: Shrub climate's spoilt

indicators.note: something spoilt is damaged and out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word with its 's read as a plain S

explanation.surface: A gardener complains that the weather has ruined a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is ignored, so climate's supplies all eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Clematis is a climbing woody plant, loosely called a shrub, grown for its flowers.

clue.text: Expert welcoming company fellow's award

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the first word holds the next ones inside

parts.note: an ace is an expert
CO is the abbreviation for company
a lad is a young fellow

explanation.surface: A skilled professional greets a firm and a colleague receives a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: The expert's word opens up between its second and third letters to take in the firm and the fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: An accolade is an honour or prize given in recognition of merit.

clue.text: A real cost potentially — alternative to stairs

indicators.note: potentially means what the letters could become once rearranged

parts.note: all the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Installing a moving stairway instead of steps could be expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalator is a moving staircase, used in place of climbing ordinary steps.

clue.text: Line not straight in bar chart

indicators.note: in tells us the letters are sitting inside the next few words of the clue

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A graph has a curving line where straight bars are expected.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc is a curved line, part of a circle's circumference, so it is not straight.

clue.text: Wake-up call — yell, with no introduction, I constantly recalled

indicators.note: having no introduction means the opening letter is dropped
recalled means called back, so the assembled string is read backwards

parts.note: the shout without its first letter
taken as written
ever means always, constantly

explanation.surface: An alarm call that screams at me endlessly, recalled with a wince.
explanation.definitionFit: Reveille is the bugle call or signal that wakes soldiers in the morning.

clue.text: Start ignoring peripheral bits and understand objective

indicators.note: ignoring the edges means dropping the outer letters and keeping the middle

parts.note: the word minus its first and last letters
to get it is to understand

explanation.surface: Advice to begin by skipping the edges and grasping the goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' looks like an instruction to begin, but it is the word to be trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: A target is a goal or aim, the same sense as objective used as a noun.

clue.text: Talent, a little, one learner's shown inside over year

indicators.note: in a down answer, over means placed above, so the part before sits on top of the next
shown inside means placed within, so these go into the word before

parts.note: taken as written
a bit is a little
I is the Roman numeral one
L is the learner driver's plate
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A trainee's small gift is revealed over the course of a year.
explanation.walkthrough: I and L go inside BIT after its B; the 's of learner's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ability is skill or aptitude, the same as talent.

clue.text: Frank's startled expression about religious sister I accommodated

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word surrounds what follows

parts.note: gee is an exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: something accommodated is given room inside, so this letter goes into the word before

parts.note: a nun is a sister in a religious order
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Frank gasps in surprise about a nun he has put up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name, but it is the adjective; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Genuine means sincere and honest, matching frank as an adjective.

clue.text: Job worry, I hesitate to say

parts.note: care is anxiety or worry
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone nervously admits to anxiety about their work.
explanation.definitionFit: A career is a person's working occupation, loosely a job pursued over time.

clue.text: Referring to pleasant surprise in quiet place

parts.note: re means concerning or referring to
a treat is a pleasant surprise

explanation.surface: A delightful surprise awaits in a peaceful spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A retreat is a secluded, peaceful place where one goes to rest.

clue.text: Social gathering one providing buzz

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a get-together for work and company

explanation.surface: A party where someone brings the excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buzz' reads as excitement at a party, but it is the literal hum of an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A bee is both a communal gathering such as a spelling bee and a buzzing insect.

clue.text: Hat from East I associated with fellow, painstaking

indicators.note: in an across answer, starting from the east side means reading right to left, backwards

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
taken as written
a gent is a gentleman or fellow

explanation.surface: Someone from the East with a hat links up with a careful man.
explanation.definitionFit: Diligent describes someone who works with steady care and effort, a synonym of painstaking.

clue.text: Aggressive note easily seen by worker

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
something lit is illuminated and easy to see
the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: A hostile message is plainly visible to an employee.
explanation.definitionFit: Militant means combative and confrontational in pursuing a cause, close to aggressive.

clue.text: Fitting carpet evenly

indicators.note: evenly means taking the even-numbered positions, every second letter

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of carpet

explanation.surface: Laying a rug so that it sits flat and level.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt means suitable or appropriate, the same as fitting used as an adjective.

clue.text: Rather indecent — not happy

explanation.surface: Someone is displeased by something a bit rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue covers both smutty humour and a low, melancholy mood.

clue.text: Stringed instrument featuring in family reunion

indicators.note: featuring in means appearing within, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A harp-like instrument gets played at a family get-together.
explanation.definitionFit: The lyre is an ancient U-shaped instrument with strings, played by plucking.

clue.text: Poorly attired, sloppy at the outset, and last to arrive

indicators.note: something done poorly is done badly, so these letters are put in a muddled order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the outset is the beginning, so only the opening letter of the preceding word is taken

parts.note: first letter of sloppy

explanation.surface: A badly dressed, scruffy latecomer turns up last.
explanation.definitionFit: Tardiest is the superlative of tardy, late, so the one who arrives after everyone else.
